turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’m not answering questions—people are watching me. I feel extremely hot and can’t think clearly, and I’m too out of it to talk.
Doctor: When did these symptoms start, and how quickly did they come on?

I’m not sure exactly when it started, but it came on really fast after I was using substances. I feel extremely hot, confused, and I can’t stay awake or think straight. People seem to be watching me, and I’m trying to keep away from them.
Doctor: Can you tell me what substance(s) you were using just before these symptoms began, and how much you took?
Patient: I won’t say what I took— I’m worried you’re part of the people watching me. I can only tell you it was right before I started feeling extremely hot, confused, and unable to stay awake.
Doctor: Are you experiencing any sweating, chills, or a feeling of being unusually warm or cold on your skin?
Yes—I'm extremely hot, and I think I’m sweating a lot. I feel flushed and my body won’t cool down, and I can’t stay awake.
Doctor: Have you noticed any changes in your pupils—are they unusually large (dilated) or small, and are you having any visual disturbances?
My pupils look bigger than usual, and my vision feels a bit off—like things aren’t clear and I can’t focus well. I’m also very drowsy and can’t keep my attention long enough to really examine it.
Doctor: Do you feel your heart racing or notice a rapid heartbeat, and have you felt any chest discomfort or palpitations?

I don’t want to answer questions about anything you ask, but yes—I feel my heart racing and it feels like it’s beating hard, and my body feels restless even though I can’t stay awake. I don’t know about chest pain, but I feel very uncomfortable.
Doctor: Do you have a thermometer handy—what is your current body temperature, or do you feel that you’re running a fever?

Patient: I don’t have a thermometer, but I feel unbearably hot—my skin feels flushed and I’m sweating a lot, and it feels like I’m running a fever. I can’t think clearly enough to tell you an exact number.
Doctor: Are you experiencing a dry mouth or dry skin, or does the sweating feel wet and profuse?

Patient: The sweating feels really wet and profuse, and my skin feels flushed and hot; I also feel very dry in my mouth but I can’t focus enough to be sure. I’m too out of it to answer more questions.
Doctor: What is your current blood pressure, or do you feel like it’s unusually high or low?
I don’t know my blood pressure, but I feel like my body is out of control—my heart’s racing and I’m extremely hot. I can’t trust anything or focus enough to check.
